remaining: Historical version-1 qualification: Glass uses a coupled fixed-pivot pendulum and rotating-prism solve, shared fixtures, friction, adaptive swept contacts and worker isolation. Packed correction and trial-cache cleanup preserve 192 sampled physical states, independent geometry samples and per-case physical summaries exactly. All eight 12-second presets, 29 focused tests, TypeScript and then-current WebGPU desktop checks pass. Maximum accepted overlap is 0.207 mm with no unresolved sweeps. Three captured dense correction inputs show 1.212–1.218x isolated kernel speedups with passing controls; sparse cases meet the declared absolute overhead limits. Whole-solver and renderer-inclusive performance remain unqualified. Earlier accepted and failed attempts are preserved.

Preceding release pass (before the version-2 kernel change): Glass presentation now interpolates received poses, requests one to four fixed ticks according to response cost, and skips hidden fragment geometry. The final source passes 37 focused tests and TypeScript; a loaded-contact fixture releases without cached-friction attraction. Collision/model/material/pendulum/fixture source match the pre-investigation baseline. Two exact CPU candidates failed timing qualification and were not selected. No new solver CPU or FPS gain is claimed.

Version 2 removes coincident manifold supports, matches previous local anchors one to one, and invalidates support on dynamic/static transitions. The integrated source passes 45 focused tests and TypeScript; all eight presets pass over 11,520 ticks and 192 independent sample times with maximum accepted overlap 0.311 mm, independent overlap 0.199 mm and zero unresolved sweeps. The 0.5 mm gate is unchanged; trajectories differ and peak overlap is not improved over version 1. A constrained slider shows first-order stopping-distance convergence and no kinetic-energy gain. Free-rotation/pile frictional work, general contact convergence, calibration and controlled whole-solver performance remain open.

Folded sheets, other crushing material studies, contact/frictional-work convergence, physical calibration and interactive performance acceptance remain. The JavaScript glass implementation does not complete native fragment promotion.

The subsequent SAT and pair-order study preserves five experimental candidates without changing the live solver. Float64 pair storage matches all eight v2 physical presets (11,520 ticks, 192 samples). Bitmap pair ordering passes 51 focused tests and 32 complete-state witnesses plus 12 restored ticks, but its own full preset matrix remains pending. An unchanged-source calibration exposes a same-process timing confound. Independent-process dense local gates pass, while the complete intact-panel, p95 and unchanged/sham gates do not; no new production CPU or FPS gain is selected. Retained measurements and corrected calibration remain available for further work.

The source passes 51 focused tests and all eight 12-second presets over 11,520 ticks and 192 independent samples; accepted overlap is at most 0.200 mm, independent overlap 0.1725 mm, with no unresolved sweeps. The candidate is not selected, the live source is unchanged, and no new full-preset or browser run is claimed. A fresh 1440-tick radial census matches all 24 stored v3 physical samples. A 338-body contact group and measured residual vertex motion limit immediate sleeping opportunities. Scalar time/iteration refinement reduces normal residual, while an experimental local normal-patch solver passes 35 corrected-source checks and an analytical support regression but does not justify fewer global iterations in the dense pile. It remains unselected; complete corrected-source suite, full-preset, browser and controlled matched-accuracy runtime acceptance are not claimed. Global contact convergence and physical calibration remain open.

The revised packed-velocity experiment passes 55 focused tests, strict module TypeScript, 1128 complete-tick deep comparisons and all eight physical presets over 11520 ticks with 192 v3 sampled-state matches. Both dense candidate mean/p95 gates and the intact absolute-overhead gates pass across 360 fresh serial processes, but both dense sham intervals and all intact unchanged-control/sham intervals fail calibration. Point estimates 1.1306x and 1.1749x remain unqualified; no packed code was installed. Earlier failed timing and signed-zero harness records are preserved. A new performance campaign needs stable unchanged controls under verified quieter conditions. Concurrent liquid-study/shared-app changes are preserved; current-app integration, settling convergence, broad controls/seeds and physical calibration remain open.

The final eight-iteration candidate reduces normal residual 53.66 percent and median actual vertex motion 29.86 percent against scalar eight, passing the fixed mathematical screen. Every tested four-or-fewer-iteration candidate fails motion/energy limits. Twelve final-source focused tests and strict module TypeScript pass; 1140 observed/unobserved and 600 disabled-candidate/v3 complete-tick comparisons hold. items.enhancement: Extend reinforced concrete from persistent bridging constraints to bond-slip and pullout behavior with measured reinforcement/concrete interface parameters.

items.enhancement: Add conservative hierarchical-depth occlusion culling for sufficiently large opaque scenes after frustum culling.
items.acceptance: Urban/warehouse scenes reduce GPU work; camera cuts, moving occluders, and disocclusion show no visible popping; small scenes can bypass it.

items.enhancement: Generate visible instance lists and indirect draw arguments on GPU, grouped by geometry/material class, with a direct-draw fallback.

remaining: GPU stable material lists and indirect arguments are implemented without count readback. Frustum/occlusion visibility filtering and general geometry batches remain.

remaining: Direct and partitioned output matches exactly for 18 tested count/MSAA combinations. The path remains opt-in pending a controlled complete-frame crossover across target adapters.

items.enhancement: Cache static shadow contributions and update dynamic casters separately; fit shadow coverage to the active experiment and invalidate on relevant light/scene changes.

remaining: Unchanged whole-caster passes are cached in raw WebGPU. Separate static/dynamic maps, scene-fit coverage and the Studio renderer remain.

items.acceptance: GPU savings exceed added geometry/encoding cost; test both sparse scenes and heavy material overlap.
